svg.title: Bounded restricted charts and the Hecke-lisse image
svg.desc: Perfect local Nakayama and cotangent cancellation give finite exterior models. Actual bounded affine and frame descent lifts universal coefficients into the ind-connection category. Full proper D-module self-duality recovers the parameterized eigencomparison, and continuous coefficient integration gives Hecke-lisse membership. Unbounded scalar and completion examples retain the precise scope; nilpotent support requires additional geometric arguments.
svg.text: Bounded charts give universal ind-connection coefficients
Complex projective curves; all connective DG parameters and unbounded automorphic inputs.
1. Cotangent cancellation gives an actual finite local model — BLI.1–BLI.10
L(A/C) perfect, Tor amplitude [−1,0]; H⁰(A) finite type, each H⁻ⁱ(A) finite.
At x: split the finite degree −1 space as U ⊕ J, J = image from degree −2.
Polynomial syzygies eliminate J after inverting a determinant nonzero at x.
A[f⁻¹] ≃ P′[ε₁,…,εᵣ], |εᵢ| = −1, dεᵢ = gᵢ; hence Hʲ = 0 for j < −r.
A finite open cover gives one bound for A; the gᵢ need not form a regular sequence.
2. The actual bounded affine presentation retains every DG point — BLI.11–BLI.15
Each power stage A(E,n) has cohomology in [−N(E,n),0].
The bound can vary with the stage; frame-nerve products with Hˢ remain bounded.
Finite coherent cones still land in a bounded power stage: colim T = Y(restr).
I ⊗ QCoh(Y) ≃ lim I ⊗ QCoh(T); the same holds for Q and for the frame nerve.
Tensor by dualizable I preserves limits. No Ind/limit interchange is assumed.
3. Full universal descent lifts the normalized tensor functor — BLI.16–BLI.18
At each bounded stage: finite-projective tensor coefficients lift from Q to I.
Full faithfulness lifts all tensor, scalar, symmetry and higher comparisons.
E(V) belongs to A ⊗ I; pullback gives the lift on every connective DG algebra.
The whole categories I and Q can still differ; I need not be left-complete.
The actual operator coefficient is identified on bounded stages and descends.
4. Full kernel duality and continuous integration identify the image — BLI.19–BLI.24
D(X) is self-dual with coevaluation Δ_*ω(X) and evaluation p_* of !-tensor.
Test with every full parameter D-module N, then recover the entire family:
H(V)(n) ≃ n ⊗ over A with E(V); the identity includes all collision maps.
Π(m) = (id ⊗ Γ!)n ⇒ H(V)(Π(m)) belongs to M ⊗ I.
For every finite I: H(vec V)(Π(m)) belongs to M ⊗ I(X)⊗ᴵ.
Nilpotent support and original-field regularity require further geometric proofs.
5. Even cells and unbounded scalars do not obstruct the finite lift — BLI.25–BLI.31
dη = dθ = x², db = θ−η: the (b,θ−η) pair contracts exactly.
h(bⁿ(θ−η)) = bⁿ⁺¹/(n+1); the result is C[x,η], dη = x².
A = C[z] ⊗ Λ(α,β), |z| = −2; u(e₁)=βe₂ and u(e₂)=αe₁.
u²(e₁)=αβe₁; u²(e₂)=−αβe₂; u³=0 while u²≠0.
The full scalar action is retained: rank two over A, with a uniform nilpotence bound.
6. The completed category still contains extra objects — BLI.32–BLI.34
On P¹: B = T(u), |u| = −1, v=u²; I is the v-torsion subcategory of Mod(B).
L = B[v⁻¹] ⊗ C[z] ≠ 0; v is invertible, so L is outside I with scalars.
Each τ≥⁻ⁿL is v-torsion, but its inverse limit in Q is L.
L ⊗ over C[z] with C = B[v⁻¹] has nonzero cohomology in every integer degree.
It is not a finite-perfect coefficient. The normalized functor comparison still holds.
Exact proofs: §§3.194–3.204, BLI.1–BLI.34; Solutions3.DJ–3.DL.
Categorical Hecke-lisse framework: AGKRRV, arXiv:2010.01906v2, §14.1.
